$comment: BASELINE OF KNOWN, UNFIXED VIOLATIONS — NOT AN EXCLUSION LIST.
It is now EMPTY. Every fixture in the corpus produces zero observable mutations of
page-owned DOM, and the suite asserts that by equality — so this file's only remaining
job is to fail the build if anything ever comes back.
The suite asserts the violation set EQUALS this baseline, exactly:
- a NEW violation fails the build (a regression)
- a violation that DISAPPEARS also fails the build, telling you to tighten this file
That second half is what makes this a ratchet rather than a mute button. Entries may only
ever be REMOVED, and removing one means the corresponding ADR 0001 site is fixed. Adding
an entry to make CI green is the thing CLAUDE.md forbids.
THE ONE CARVE-OUT: a NEW fixture starts with no baseline, so its first run is
indistinguishable from a regression and the suite correctly refuses it. Recording its
entries is allowed ONLY when every one of them is a violation already catalogued in
ADR 0001 and already present in other fixtures — i.e. the fixture found nothing new. If a
new fixture surfaces a violation no other fixture has, that is a discovery, and it gets an
ADR entry and an issue before it gets a baseline line. With the baseline at zero there is
nothing left that qualifies, so in practice this is now closed.
How it got here:
E1 imported the engine with 169 entries across the corpus — the fourteen sites
catalogued in docs/adr/0001-upstream-purity-audit.md.
E2 step 0 (ADR 0001 items 7, 8, 9, 10) removed 128: the data-darkreader-mode and
-scheme writes on <html>, the MV3 proxy handshake attribute, and the transient <meta>
instance marker plus lock. 23 fixtures dropped to zero.
E2 step 2 (ADR 0001 items 1-5 and 6, ADR 0006) removed the remaining 41: the inline
`style` attribute writes, the `data-darkreader-inline-*` markers, and the SVG inversion
attribute. Theming an inline-styled element no longer touches it at all — the
declarations are read and matched by selectors in a sheet we own.
The entry worth naming is `contenteditable-editor.html`: an editor that serialized our
writes into its own document model on every mutation, which is the Google Sheets failure
this project exists to prevent. It reads zero because there is nothing to serialize, not
because anything was excluded.
With this at zero, every fixture also runs the byte-identity assertion — serialized HTML
and page-owned stylesheet text — which the non-empty entries used to skip.
